1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	Guidance for working in this repository.
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	Spring PetClinic REST, converted from Spring `@RestController` classes to
8	**OfficeFloor function injection**. Spring's DI, security, persistence and DTOs are
9	unchanged; only the request handling is now explicit function orchestration.
10	
11	<!-- https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md -->
12	@AGENTS.md
13

1	## OfficeFloor REST endpoints
2	
3	Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
4	OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
5	pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.
6	
7	- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
8	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
9	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
10	  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
11	- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
12	  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
13	- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
14	- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
15	- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
16	- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
17	
18	### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
19	
20	The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
21	
22	`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
23	
24	```yaml
25	# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
26	# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
27	validate:
28	  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
29	  next: load
30	load:
31	  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
32	  next: apply
33	apply:
34	  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
35	  govern: [ transaction ]
36	  next: save
37	save:
38	  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
39	  govern: [ transaction ]
40	  next: respond
41	respond:
42	  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
43	```
44	
45	```java
46	// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
47	public class ValidateOwner {
48	  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
49	    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
50	  }
51	}
52	public class LoadOwner {
53	  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
54	      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
55	    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
56	    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
57	    ownerOut.set(owner);
58	  }
59	}
60	public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
61	  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
62	    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
63	    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
64	  }
65	}
66	public class SaveOwner {
67	  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
68	    repository.save(owner);
69	  }
70	}
71	public class RespondWithOwner {
72	  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
73	    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
74	  }
75	}
76	```
77	
78	`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
79	
80	```yaml
81	handle:
82	  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
83	```
84	
85	```java
86	public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
87	  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
88	      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
89	    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
90	  }
91	}
92	```
93	
94	### Step wiring
95	
96	Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
97	point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
98	method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
99	`method:`.
100	
101	- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
102	  as `@Parameter T`.
103	- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
104	  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
105	  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
106	
107	### Function parameters
108	
109	Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
110	
111	- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
112	- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
113	- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
114	  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
115	  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
116	- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
117	  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
118	
119	### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
120	
121	Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
122	into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
123	
124	- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
125	- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
126	  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
127	- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
128	  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
129	
130	### Naming
131	
132	Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
133	absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
134	publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
135	`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
136	
137	Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
138	responder. Steps in between work with entities.
139	
140	### Request body and validation
141	
142	- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
143	  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
144	  first step publishes it as a variable.
145	- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
146	  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
147	  invalid body can return 400.
148	
149	### Transactions
150	
151	`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
152	listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
153	the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
154	
155	### Errors
156	
157	Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
158	Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
159	`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
160	`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
161	anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. Stored and returned in E.164 form (a
            leading '+' followed by 8-15 digits); national numbers default to the '+61' country code.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional. When present it must be a 4-digit number valid for the city's region (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned as given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional on create; when omitted the server's current date is used. The effective date must fall on a business day, so a Saturday or Sunday (whether supplied or defaulted) is rolled forward to the next Monday.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: The owner's date of birth, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional. When present, the
            owner's ageBand is derived from it against the registrationDate.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner already
            has the same last name and address (they share a household). Optional; defaults to false.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Franklin, George'
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'G.F.'
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of city, LAST3 the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'SYD-SMI-0007'
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'SYD-SMI-0007-M26'
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits contained in the owner's customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              readOnly: true
              example: 4
            householdId:
              title: Household ID

The household is now keyed on **(lastName, postcode)** and derived deterministically, so shared households need no stored link.

**`CountHouseholdMembers`** — the household-size count now keys off the computed `householdId` (postcode-based).

**`OwnerIdentity.key` / `OwnerMapper`** — the `householdId` and `identityKey` response fields now derive from postcode instead of address.

**`openapi.yml`** — updated the `sharesHousehold` and `householdId` descriptions to match the new (lastName, postcode) semantics.

- Same lastName + postcode ⇒ same `householdId` automatically (no stored link).
- A second owner in an existing household ⇒ **409**, unless `sharesHousehold` ⇒ created as a declared member.

## What changed

The household is now keyed on **(lastName, postcode)** and derived deterministically, so shared households need no stored link.

**`Household.id(lastName, postcode)`** — now takes postcode instead of address and returns the **first 12 hex chars** of `SHA-256(normalize(lastName) + "|" + postcode)` (was 16 hex over `lastName|address`). `normalize` (trim/collapse-whitespace/lowercase) still applies to the last name; postcode is used as given (null-guarded to `""`).

**`RequireUniqueIdentity`** (the duplicate block) — now also rejects a **household duplicate** (an existing owner with the same computed `householdId`) as **409**, *bypassed when the request sets `sharesHousehold`*. The pre-existing contact-key (telephone+email) collision check is kept — `sharesHousehold` does not bypass that, since a declared member is still a distinct contact.

**`FlagPossibleDuplicate`** — a **declared member** (`sharesHousehold=true`) is no longer flagged: `possibleDuplicate=false`, `possibleDuplicateOf=null`. It reads `sharesHousehold` via the published `OwnerFieldsDto` variable. (Any non-declared owner sharing lastName+postcode is now rejected upstream, so this is the only path that shares a household and survives.)

**`CountHouseholdMembers`** — the household-size count now keys off the computed `householdId` (postcode-based).

**`OwnerIdentity.key` / `OwnerMapper`** — the `householdId` and `identityKey` response fields now derive from postcode instead of address.

**`openapi.yml`** — updated the `sharesHousehold` and `householdId` descriptions to match the new (lastName, postcode) semantics.

## Behaviour now matches the spec
- Same lastName + postcode ⇒ same `householdId` automatically (no stored link).
- A second owner in an existing household ⇒ **409**, unless `sharesHousehold` ⇒ created as a declared member.
- A declared member is **not** flagged as a possible duplicate.
- Duplicate detection and household sizing both key off the computed `householdId`.

The `AcceptanceTest` (`coreSameLastNameAndPostcodeShareHouseholdId`) — which uses `sharesHousehold` to bypass the block and asserts equal `householdId` for same lastName+postcode and differing for a different lastName — passes.
